title: Delegated Authorization Provenance and Forensic Checklist
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the minimal provenance requirements, audit collection checklist, and forensic evidence handling procedures for delegated authorization events in Redwood Inference. It covers attribute-based delegation, service-to-service tokens, cross-tenant delegation, and short-lived elevation flows. The goal is to ensure that delegated decisions are reproducible, auditable, and admissible for incident response and regulatory evidence.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood systems that perform delegated authorization, including:
  - API gateway and edge authorization (ext-authN/Z services)
  - Internal service role brokers and attribute brokers
  - Short-lived elevation flows (just-in-time admin, emergency access)
  - External SSO/OIDC assertions and SCIM-provisioned attributes
- Does not replace application-level logging; it mandates minimum fields and retention for audit-grade provenance.

Key Ownership

- Data custodian: Identity & Access Management (IAM) team
- Evidence steward: Security response & forensics team
- Operational owner: Platform SRE
- Retention policy owner: Compliance & legal

High-level Requirements

1) Provenance must include an unambiguous decision record for every delegated authorization event. Minimum fields:
  - event_id (UUID v4)
  - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  - subject_id (persona or service_id performing the action)
  - subject_type (human | service | federated)
  - actor_assertion (token / SAML/OIDC subject - hashed)
  - asserted_attributes (list: roles, groups, org_unit, custom claims)
  - delegation_chain (ordered list of issuer_ids or delegation_event_ids)
  - resource_id and resource_type
  - action or permission requested
  - decision (allow | deny | deferred) and decision_reason_code
  - policy_version and policy_sha256
  - evaluator_service (service name and version)
  - correlation_id (request path trace id)

2) Immutable audit capture: all decision records must be written to the immutable audit pipeline within 5 seconds of decision issuance. The pipeline must append and not update records.

3) Evidence packaging: when an investigation is opened, produce a signed evidence bundle containing the decision records, related raw logs, and a chain-of-custody manifest.

Detailed Checklist (Operational)

A. Pre-deployment (engineering / SDLC)
  1. Design: Ensure all authorization decision points produce the minimum decision record fields (see above).
  2. Code review: Security reviewer validates that any changes to the evaluator or attribute handling preserve deterministic policy_versioning and expose policy_sha256 in logs.
  3. Test: Add synthetic test that asserts every auth decision emitted during test toggles includes event_id and correlation_id and is forwarded to the audit sink.
  4. Deployment checklist: Flag any change that introduces new attribute sources (e.g., new SCIM feed) for re-certification of mapping and retention.

B. Runtime (SRE / Platform)
  1. Latency SLA: Decision records must be persisted to audit sink within 5s 99th percentile. Alert if 5s SLA violated for >1% of requests in a 5m window.
  2. Sampling & completeness: No sampling permitted for delegation events affecting admin, billing, or cross-tenant access. For non-admin, ensure at-least 100% metadata capture (event header) and allow sampling of verbose attribute dumps only under controlled flags.
  3. Integrity: Audit sink signs blocks with HSM-backed keys on rollup intervals (configurable, default 15m).

C. Incident response (security response / forensics)
  Step 1 — Triage:
    - Capture the alert ID, implicated resource_id, and time window.
    - Query decision records by resource_id and correlation_id to enumerate delegation chains.
  Step 2 — Evidence collection:
    - Freeze relevant audit partitions (timebox ± 2 minutes around the incident).
    - Export decision records, raw evaluator traces, and the attribute broker request/response pairs.
    - Export relevant network-level logs (ingress gateway, service mesh mTLS sessions) and application request/response samples.
  Step 3 — Forensics checklist (order matters):
    1. Export decision records (immutable) as newline-delimited JSON; verify event counts against live metrics.
    2. Export attribute snapshots used in each decision (hashed PII if applicable).
    3. Export original token assertions (SAML/OIDC/JWT) with token id_prefix; do not store full tokens in evidence bundle unless legally required — instead store hashed token and token metadata.
    4. Generate chain-of-custody manifest (see template below).
    5. Sign the evidence bundle using the evidence steward key and record signature metadata in the manifest.

Evidence Bundle Template (manifest fields)

- bundle_id: string
- produced_by: team/service name
- produced_at: ISO8601
- custody_chain: ordered list of custodians with timestamps
- items: list of item entries (item_id, type, path, hash_sha256)
- signature: base64(signature)
- signature_key_id: KMS key alias

Retention and Data Residency Controls

- Retention windows:
  - Delegated decision records (immutable): default 7 years for enterprise tenants, 2 years for internal system accounts.
  - Verbose attribute dumps (PII-sensitive): default 90 days; must be redacted or hashed prior to long-term retention.
  - Evidence bundles produced for investigations: retained per legal hold instructions; otherwise archived for 10 years.
- Residency: Maintain tenant residency tags on every decision record so queries can be scoped by geo/tenant. Cross-border copies require approval from Compliance and Legal.

Privacy and PII handling

- Never include full raw credentials or unencrypted PII in the audit sink. Always hash or redact subject tokens (store token_id and token_hash).
- Attribute broker must provide attribute classification (sensitive|non-sensitive) exported with every attribute snapshot.

Exception and Risk Handling

- Emergency elevation flows: must emit an escalation_event with reason_code, approver_id, and audit_ticket_id. These events are preserved without sampling.
- Control exceptions: any exception to retention or residency must be recorded as a control-exception entry with owner, justification, expiration, and compensating controls.

Query Patterns and Forensic Playbooks

- Common queries (examples):
  - Find all delegation events for subject_id over last 24 hours:
    SELECT * FROM decision_records WHERE subject_id = '<id>' AND timestamp >= now()-interval '24 hours';
  - Reconstruct delegation chain for correlation_id:
    SELECT * FROM decision_records WHERE correlation_id = '<cid>' ORDER BY timestamp ASC;

- Forensic playbook: recreate the decision path, then validate attributes at each hop against attribute broker snapshots. Any divergence suggests stale attributes or replayed assertions.

Automation and Tooling

- Audit sink exposes an API to produce signed evidence bundles for a given timebox and filter set.
- Evidence packaging CLI example:
  redwood-forensics export --start 2026-05-20T08:30:00Z --end 2026-05-20T09:00:00Z --filters 'resource_id=svc-uploads' --output /tmp/evidence-bundle-20260520.tar.gz

Sample decision record (newline-delimited JSON example)

{"event_id":"8f3f6b2c-2a6a-4f9e-9d3a-1d2b6c4e7f00","timestamp":"2026-05-20T08:42:11.123Z","subject_id":"alice@redwood.com","subject_type":"human","actor_assertion_hash":"sha256:ab12...","asserted_attributes":"[\"role:service-admin\",\"group:infra\"]","delegation_chain":"[\"svc-identity-broker:2026-01-15\"]","resource_id":"tenant-42:project-9:dataset-7","resource_type":"dataset","action":"read","decision":"allow","decision_reason_code":"policy-match-317","policy_version":"v2026-01-12","policy_sha256":"sha256:fe34...","evaluator_service":"auth-evaluator:v3.4.1","correlation_id":"trace-7a9d"}

(When exporting for evidence, include a signed checksum of the NDJSON file and record the signature in the manifest.)

Audit Quality Metrics

- Completeness rate: percent of auth decisions containing the required minimum fields; target >= 99.95% monthly.
- Ingestion lag: 99th percentile ingestion to immutable sink <= 5s.
- Tamper detection: number of unsigned blocks or failed HSM sign operations = 0 monthly.

Implementation Notes and Gotchas

- Policy versioning: Use content-addressable policy identifiers (SHA256 of canonicalized policy) to avoid ambiguity when policy text is reformatted.
- Token rotation: when token formats change, preserve mapping from token_id to token_schema in a versioned registry.
- High cardinality attributes: avoid emitting raw high-cardinality identifiers into the audit sink; instead emit hashed identifiers and separate mapping stores protected by stricter access controls.

Appendices

A. Chain-of-Custody manifest example (NDJSON entry)
  {"manifest_item_id":"item-01","path":"decision_records/2026-05-20.ndjson","hash_sha256":"fe34...","collected_by":"redwood-forensics","collected_at":"2026-05-20T09:05:00Z"}

B. Escalation matrix
  - Tier 1: IAM oncall (first response, confirm scope)
  - Tier 2: Security response (lead forensic collection)
  - Tier 3: Legal & Compliance (for evidence preservation and external disclosure)

C. References
  - Internal: authn-authz/design/attribute-broker-architecture (link)
  - Internal: audit-logging/immutable-audit-store (link)
  - External: NIST SP 800-92 (Guide to Computer Security Log Management)
